newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo central bank keeps discount rate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Yugo central bank keeps discount rate unchanged.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) left its key discount rate for April unchanged at 2.5 percent per month, or an annual 35.04 percent, a central bank official told Reuters on Monday.
The NBY sharply cut the discount rate in March from 4.5 percent per month, following a significant slowdown in monthly inflation in February and stabilizing monetary developments.
Retail prices in February were only 0.6 percent up on January when they rose 1.4 percent against December.
The discount rate, NBY's key instrument in regulating market liquidity, was kept unchanged at 4.5 percent since June 1996.

The central bank sets its discount rate each month using a basket that includes interest rates on the open money market and its short-term bonds, price rises, expected monetary developments, credit demand and money supply.
